clue.text: See 12
Call to hug tree, sounding rough

indicators.note: to hug something is to wrap around it, so the call encloses the tree

parts.note: to call out is to cry
the oak is a common tree

explanation.surface: Someone shouts while embracing a tree, their voice hoarse.
explanation.definitionFit: A croaky voice is hoarse and rasping, the way a frog's call sounds.

clue.text: Seed that's old removed from a loch

indicators.note: something removed from another is taken out of it, here the abbreviation for old leaves the loch

parts.note: a loch here is Loch Lomond, the large Scottish lake, giving A plus LOMOND

explanation.surface: A seed is said to have been taken out of a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Loch Lomond is Scotland's best-known lake; with A in front and its O taken out, A LOMOND loses a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The edible kernel of the almond tree is botanically its seed, eaten as a nut.

clue.text: Quit a golf game to wander idly

parts.note: to kick a habit is to quit it
a round is one complete game of golf

explanation.surface: Someone gives up a game of golf and drifts off aimlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick around is an informal phrasal verb for drifting about with no purpose.

clue.text: Down to make an error

definitions.meaning: down in the sense of soft light feathers or fuzz
to bungle a line or a shot, a slip by a performer or player

explanation.surface: Feeling low enough to make a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluff is soft downy fibre, and to fluff something is to botch it.

clue.text: See 12
Player, a giant with red dicky

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for shaky or unreliable, so the letters are unsettled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor described as a giant who has a dodgy red item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dicky' (British slang for weak or faulty, as in a dicky heart) signals rearranging A GIANT RED.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is an actor who specialises in tragic roles, and players are actors.

clue.text: Norse collection needed, say, regularly

indicators.note: regularly means take letters at even intervals, here every second letter of the two words

explanation.surface: A Norse anthology is required, as one might say, on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of 'needed say'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edda is the medieval Icelandic compilation of Norse myths and poems.

clue.text: Become angry: prayer causing breach of faith, unfortunately

indicators.note: a breach is a break, so the prayer breaks into the other letters and sits inside them
things gone wrong are disordered, so the letters of faith are rearranged

parts.note: an Ave (Ave Maria) is a prayer to the Virgin Mary

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper when a prayer seems to betray their belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges the belief word into HAFIT; 'causing breach of' sets the Latin prayer inside, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw a fit is an idiom for losing one's temper explosively.

clue.text: Woman carrying pig lacking tail and hair

indicators.note: lacking its tail means the final letter of the word for pig is dropped

parts.note: pork is pig meat, and pig is used for it
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A woman holds a pig that has no tail, plus some hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A portress is a female porter, and porters carry luggage, so a woman carrying fits.

clue.text: With lead removed, massive like a trace metal?

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter, which is taken off here

parts.note: cosmic means vast or massive in scale

explanation.surface: A question about whether something huge resembles a metal found in tiny amounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmic means relating to osmium, a rare element, and the question mark flags it as one example of a trace metal.

clue.text: As may be an entrance at university, somewhere in Hampshire

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university, in British usage
Andover is a town in Hampshire, a county in southern England

explanation.surface: A doorway at a college in a southern English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Garage doors are often of the type that swings upward and back, so an entrance may be built this way.

clue.text: Nearest and dearest recollection of standard socialist leader once

parts.note: one's nearest and dearest are one's kin, close family

indicators.note: read as re-collection, gathering the letters up again in a different order

parts.note: a standard is a flag
red is a common label for a socialist

explanation.surface: Family memories of the flag of an old socialist chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred the Great was a ninth-century ruler of Wessex, a historic leader of the English.

clue.text: Party organiser's pretty funny — a reasonable chance

parts.note: fair means pretty, good-looking
a funny is a joke, and so is a crack
the whip organises a parliamentary party's voting, and the possessive reads as 'of the' plus that title

explanation.surface: A party planner is amusingly attractive, which offers some hope.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's turns into 'of the': the party organiser's becomes OF THE WHIP, the Whip being the official who keeps a party's MPs in line.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a fair opportunity or equal treatment, a decent go at something.

clue.text: Flame flickering over Bela Lugosi say, villain

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another sits above it, coming first
a flickering flame moves unsteadily, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: Bela Lugosi, who played Dracula, is an example of an actor

explanation.surface: A flickering flame lights the horror star, cast as a villain.
explanation.definitionFit: A malefactor is a wrongdoer or criminal, a fitting synonym for a villain.

clue.text: Plots extremely pathetic and scenario is ludicrous

indicators.note: something ludicrous is absurd, so the letters go wild and are reordered
the extremes of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Plans that are wholly pitiful and a scenario that is absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes P and C from 'pathetic'; 'ludicrous' rearranges them with SCENARIO IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Conspiracies are secret schemes, and plots is a common synonym for them.

clue.text: See 24
Responsible, short advert written up in message

indicators.note: one piece in another is put inside it

parts.note: a cable is a telegram, a message

indicators.note: in a down clue written up means read from bottom to top, backwards
short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a plug is a piece of promotion, an advert

explanation.surface: Someone is to blame for a brief advertisement placed in a telegram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the advert word to PLU, and 'written up' reads it upward, as suits a down clue, before 'in' places it within the telegram word.
explanation.definitionFit: Culpable means deserving blame, held responsible for some fault.

clue.text: Panels only entertained by fools

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is held within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to fool someone is to con them
sole means only, as in the sole survivor

explanation.surface: Panels of experts that are merely amused by jesters.
explanation.definitionFit: Consoles are control panels, such as those holding switches and dials.

clue.text: Simple switch turned on to receive call

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so the call is held inside the jumbled letters
to switch things is to change them around, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them

explanation.surface: A basic switch is flicked on in order to take a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch' looks like a light switch but rearranges TURNED ON into UNORNTED; 'to receive' puts NAME inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no decoration or frills is plain, the sense of simple here.

clue.text: Wool top pulled up in the manner of pockets

indicators.note: to pocket something is to take it in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: à la is French for in the manner of

indicators.note: in a down clue pulled up means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle

explanation.surface: A woollen hat yanked upward in the style of pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpaca is the fine wool from the South American animal of that name.

clue.text: Saw catching top of thigh, hurt

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to have seen is to have spied

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A saw blade nicks the upper thigh and causes injury.
explanation.definitionFit: To spite someone is to deliberately hurt or upset them, past tense here.

clue.text: See 28
Sham bribe to cross border, rubbish

parts.note: cod is British slang for fake or mock, as in cod philosophy

indicators.note: to cross something is to span it, so the bribe goes across and around the border

parts.note: a sop is something given to pacify, a bribe
a wall forms a border

explanation.surface: A fake bribe to get across a frontier is nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: COD for sham or mock is a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Codswallop is British slang for nonsense, the sense of rubbish as foolish talk.

clue.text: Slave branded by one, the mark of a printer

indicators.note: a brand burned into skin sits within it, so the one is inserted

parts.note: a serf was a feudal bondsman, a slave
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A slave is branded by someone, bearing a printer's mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small stroke at the end of a letter in type, a typographic mark.

clue.text: Play totally dominant role, as might a cannibal at breakfast time?

definitions.meaning: to ... complete power over someone, to be in total control

definitions.text: as might a cannibal at breakfast time?
definitions.meaning: taken literally, a person served up on a slice of browned bread for the morning meal

explanation.surface: Dominating someone utterly, like a cannibal at the breakfast table.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to have someone completely at your mercy; literally it is a person on bread for breakfast.

clue.text: Singer, a delicate creature, going after bouncer

indicators.note: the second part goes after the first, so the bouncer comes first

parts.note: a ball is something that bounces
a deer is a graceful, delicate animal

explanation.surface: A singer and a dainty animal arrive after a nightclub doorman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncer' suggests a nightclub doorman but is a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A balladeer is a singer of ballads, a type of folk vocalist.

clue.text: See 24
Record on piano, no way for music entrepreneur

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: no way means the word way is dropped from the piano's name

parts.note: a Steinway is a famous make of piano

explanation.surface: A recording made on a piano, with no route open to a music impresario.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian Epstein was the businessman who managed the Beatles, a celebrated music entrepreneur.

clue.text: Saucy proposition that's illegal for a hooker?

parts.note: forward means cheeky or saucy in manner
to make a pass is to proposition someone

explanation.surface: A cheeky offer that a prostitute could be arrested for.
explanation.walkthrough: A hooker is a rugby forward; a throw ahead to a team-mate is illegal in rugby. The question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby a throw towards the opponents' line is against the rules for every player, a hooker included.
